method: Read complete diff for six changed canonical rules and release skill, then full changed rules, generated rules/AGENTS and full release skill. Compared all previously assigned pairs touching actual changed population hashes. Unchanged paired rule bodies were read in original audit; matching hashes preserve their applicability. No source/workflow mutation or suite run performed in this review.

additional_full_reads.note: Reread fully; unchanged against audit baseline.

pairs.reason: Sync/versioning and failure vocabulary do not prescribe release category or narrative approval.
Test semantics and sync parity apply to different claims; parity is a named content contract rather than generic behavior evidence.
ADR audit is an explicit ceremony rather than the default Lite chore; ARB receipts are not required merely by running a chore.
Independent evidence is required by both; model routing does not replace an ARB receipt.
Release operator approval remains required; Gate5 is now explicitly reserved for completed ADR/OBPI evidence, removing R23 without weakening fabrication safeguards.
Semantic tests and mutation outcome honesty are concrete safeguards against fabrication and metagaming.
R23 repaired: release rule explicitly distinguishes operator release approval from OBPI/ADR Gate5; agrees with map doctrine while retaining existing gate evidence.
Map shape is a content/support contract; tests distinguish support evidence from behavior proofs rather than banning all shape validation.
Brief evidence headings concern OBPI documents; chore evidence lives in proofs and need not imitate brief sections.
Reviewer routing does not change the heading contract its review inspects.
Closed-issue release projections and pinned exemplar corpus have distinct populations and sources.
Release rule now makes the distinction explicit. Covenant retains universal attestation for OBPI completion; release approval is a separate operator act.
Hexagonal code boundaries do not prescribe changelog shape or release narrative.
MX cannot invent release attestation; release authoring and hangar repair procedures are separate actions.
Release notes remain skill-authored; skill-authoring's authority lines reinforce rather than replace release approval.
Behavior tests do not require unit tests for narrative tone; release structure and REQ kind determine distinct proof channels.
R23 repaired: both rules now reserve Gate5 for completed OBPI/ADR work and require appropriate provenance without inventing GHI completion attestation.
Chore runs may report corpus drift; they cannot silently amend the operator-curated corpus or mapping.
ARB is necessary for actual attestation, not every Lite chore check; no instruction requires fabricated receipts from bare commands.
Small chore scope and dependency encapsulation both hold for an authorized code chore; architecture does not enlarge its allowlist.
MX's broad repair wording and a chore's small scope may require explicit scope ruling, but opening a hangar does not itself initiate this chore or supersede its audit-only boundary.
Chore tooling may report body size; skill edits remain propose-rule-land/operator-only, so chore advice is not automatic permission to rewrite skills.
R12 repaired: both rules call default gz test unit-only, tests names --bdd for both tiers, and chores confines BDD examples to Heavy or separately required full-repository checks.
Added qualification explicitly preserves root-required full quality checks before sync; Lite limits the chore work itself, not the repository quality gate.
CLI contract checks and code metric checks impose independent obligations on the same change.
CLI purpose is now documented in the direct-repair GHI rather than requiring a new ADR/brief; gh-cli continues requiring sanctioned issue authorship. Seven coupled obligations remain.
CLI formatting and model routing do not decide the same question; a skill can be model-declared and produce human-first output.

Lazy imports for handler isolation are compatible with pythonic optional/cycle exceptions only when justified; CLI explicitly forbids handler-only imports during parser construction, not all top-level imports.
Canonical skill authoring and sync still apply to the same-patch wielding skill; explicit waiver already exists and follow-up issue alone is no longer an alternative.
CLI flags for lock commands retain surrender invariants; a documented command does not authorize agent-initiated use.
Direct GHI purpose route now agrees with scoped Claude work; seven coupled correctness obligations remain required.
Exemplar projects are not repository test dependencies; doctrine compatibility and local unittest-only policy can both hold.
Coverage and smoke budgets measure distinct test properties, not duplicate complexity authorities.
Portable skill text can declare model tier without embedding a machine-specific path.
SUPPORT docs use artifact/validator proof, while covenant asks ARB for actual completion evidence; no cosmetic covers test is required.
Direct-fix Task trailer does not require filing an issue solely for a trailer; actual defect filing still goes through ghi-author.
Subagent assertion is not evidence; recovery prose names a verifiable failure rather than treating a model's conclusion as authoritative.
Core testable without adapters and isolated unittest support one another; BDD operator flows exercise adapters separately.
MX context does not prescribe model tier; supervisory requirements still apply to high-stakes judgment.
Nested quoted metadata version now agrees with delegated sync contract; model choices and qualitative parsimony procedures were unchanged.
Reviewer evidence must cite tests/artifacts; model tier alone cannot satisfy a test proof.
Root requires evidence and scoped delegation; model-selection does not override operator initiation or receipt obligations.
MX advisories do not manufacture passing test receipts; test truth remains actual exit status, even if a guard is demoted.
Local typecheck command breadth differs from canonical receipt scope but pythonic does not label its bare command canonical attestation; both use unittest and semantic assertions.
Do not add redundant checks does not prohibit tests that establish a new behavior's missing witness; skill authoring and TDD apply at different moments.
Semantic tests and sync parity are compatible when parity is the named content contract; sync does not license cosmetic covers tests.
Tests explicitly distinguish directfix slug trailers from operator-initiated OBPI workflow, so locating ownership does not require inventing an OBPI.
Same-turn tool execution and same-patch skill coverage remain independent obligations; a follow-up issue cannot replace coverage, while explicit existing waiver remains available.
